item.title: Pavement blocked with commercial skips, 30th July
item.description:
Two commercial skips have been placed on the pavement by the business operating out of the railway arches at 7A Sutherland Walk, SE17. The skips are directly opposite a cycle hanger, meaning the area is already restricted. The presence of the skips is restricting access and is particularly dangerous for the elderly and parents with prams, etc. One skip has been present for a few months, the second has recently appeared. As well as blocking the pavement, the skips are encouraging fly tipping and impacting on me and other local residents.

item.title: Confirmed Subsidence Claim & Overhead Cable Hazard — Council Tree, 30th July
item.description:
Dear Bexley Tree and Woodland Team, I am writing to formally request the complete removal of the Council-owned trees and overgrown vegetation located on the boundary of Danson Park, directly adjacent to my property. My Buildings Insurance provider has officially confirmed active subsidence affecting my property. Foundation monitoring is currently being conducted by insurance engineers. The active root system of this Council tree is strongly suspected of causing moisture abstraction and foundation movement. My insurer is preparing a formal liability notice to be issued to Bexley Council regarding this structural damage. The roots of these trees are actively growing into, under, and over my boundary fence. The pressure from the expanding roots is causing severe structural destabilisation, tilting, and physical destruction of the fence, putting it at imminent risk of collapse. The upper canopy of the tree has reached a height where heavy branches are actively entangling and pressing against the overhead telephone and broadband drop cables attached to my roof/fascia board. During high winds, the sway of these branches risks snapping essential utility lines and causing structural damage to the roof anchoring points of my property. The lower overhanging branches feature sharp thorns that encroach significantly onto my primary access pathway. I have already sustained physical cuts and bleeding while attempting to access my home. This creates a continuous public safety hazard for occupants and visitors. It’s been happening about 6 months ago. Cause I don’t know whether is subsidence or not, so I contacted the house insurance company to monitor. It’s find out the trees root damaging my property. Requested Action: 1. Completely remove / fell the tree(s) and extract/treat the root systems to stop further damage to my home's foundations and boundary fence. 2. Clear all overgrown weeds, brush, and wild vegetation along this section of the boundary. 3.Send a Tree Officer to conduct an urgent on-site inspection to assess the fence and foundation damage. Insurance Claim Reference: Aviva (4504093991) I have attached photograph evidence showing: Given the potential legal liabilities and safety risks involved, I look forward to your prompt response to confirm a date for an urgent site inspection. Yours sincerely, Tsz Fung Tsui 61 Danson Lane, welling, DA16 2BQ 07723068815 roughtsui@gmail.com

Nearest road to the pin placed on the map (automatically generated by OpenStreetMap): Danson Lane, Welling, Greater London
Report on FixMyStreet
